raw_case_text:
The case concerns a 58-year-old male patient who underwent aortic valve replacement on December 17, 2021 for severe aortic valve insufficiency and received warfarin anticoagulation postoperatively. On January 7, 2022, the patient developed mobility impairment of the right limb. A cranial computed tomography (CT) scan showed cerebral infarction, so antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy was administered. On January 12, the patient developed a fever with a maximum body temperature of 39.8 C. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) showed normal mechanical aortic valve function after mechanical aortic valve replacement. The patient presented an aortic root lesion (abscess ulceration with multiple superfluous formations and localized aortic root entrapment combined with an aneurysm) and segmental ventricular wall motion abnormalities. Intravenous daptomycin 500 mg was administered daily for anti-infection. The patient had recurrent fever with temperature fluctuations between 38-39 C. On February 20, the patient developed confusion, and a cranial CT scan showed a hematoma in the right frontal lobe, a subarachnoid hemorrhage in the right occipital lobe, and multiple lacunar infarctions in the bilateral basal ganglia and left paraventricular area. Pulmonary CT showed bronchitis, and 1 g of Tienam was given every 8 h in combination with 500 mg of daptomycin daily for anti-infection. On February 23, the patient developed chills and another high fever, with a maximum body temperature of 39 C, rapid breathing of 30-40 breaths per minute, and declining consciousness. For further treatment, he was transferred to our department on February 23. The patient had previous diabetes mellitus and pre-excitation syndrome and had undergone radiofrequency ablation. He entered our department with the test results as shown in Table 1. We were also provided with an electrocardiogram (Figure 1) and a transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE; Figure 2a, b). The patient had been diagnosed with cerebral infarction, cerebral hemorrhage, myocardial infarction, pulmonary infection, aortic insufficiency, IE after heart valve replacement, multiple organ dysfunction syndromes, renal insufficiency, cardiac insufficiency, abnormal coagulation function, abnormal liver function, type 2 diabetes, and anemia.
The patient was admitted with respiratory distress, a Glasgow Coma Scale of less than 8, and intermittent convulsions. A ventilator with tracheal intubation was used to assist respiration, and sedatives and sodium valproate were pumped to control epilepsy. Bronchoscopy showed normal mucosa of both bronchi, and a small amount of thin yellow-white sputum was visible at the left and right bronchial openings. Daptomycin and Tienam continued to be given to fight infection. On March 24, blood was simultaneously collected for culture and testing and sent to the hospital for inspection by ultra-multiplex PCR. The multiplex PCR results received on February 25 were as follows (Figure 3): Aspergillus flavus <1 x 102/L, Aspergillus oryzae <1 x 102/L, cytomegalovirus 2 x 102/L, G test 343.84 pg/mL, and GM 0.83. Test results indicated that the patient had endocarditis infected with Aspergillus, and the first dose of voriconazole was added at 6 mg/kg twice per day and was administered by 2 mg/day intravenous infusions maintained at 4 mg/kg. On February 28, the patient's body temperature dropped to 37.8 C, and the test results were as shown in Table 1: Blood culture results reported negative on March 2.
 Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus oryzae were detected by pathogen-targeted metagenomics next-generation sequencing (ptNGS) of the blood (87 and 25 Copies/mL), Table 2 and Figure 4a, b. The primer sequences are as shown in Table 3.
Our treatment adjustment for this patient was to report the ultra-multiplex PCR results before obtaining a negative blood culture result for 5 days and to adjust the antibiotic time schedule, which led to effective infection control, successful ventilator withdrawal, and a clear state of consciousness. The patient was subsequently transferred out of the intensive care unit. Unfortunately, in the later stage, a massive cerebral hemorrhage combined with a new cerebral infarction led to the death of the patient.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old male with a recent mechanical aortic valve replacement presented with recurrent high fevers up to 39.8 C, chills, right limb mobility impairment, tachypnea, and declining consciousness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient underwent mechanical aortic valve replacement on December 17, 2021 for severe aortic insufficiency and started warfarin. On January 7, 2022, he developed right limb mobility impairment due to cerebral infarction. On January 12, he developed recurrent fevers (up to 39.8 C) with aortic root abscess/aneurysm on TTE, persisting despite daily IV daptomycin (500 mg). On February 20, he developed confusion with right frontal hematoma, right occipital subarachnoid hemorrhage, and bilateral basal ganglia/paraventricular lacunar infarctions on cranial CT, and imipenem/cilastatin (Tienam 1 g q8h) was added. On February 23, he developed chills, fever of 39 C, tachypnea (30-40 breaths/min), and coma, prompting transfer to our ICU.
subjective.past_medical_history: Severe aortic valve insufficiency status post mechanical aortic valve replacement (December 2021), type 2 diabetes mellitus, and pre-excitation syndrome status post radiofrequency ablation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever, chills, right-sided weakness, confusion, tachypnea, and convulsions.

objective.physical_examination: Admitted to ICU on February 23 with severe respiratory distress (respiratory rate 30-40 breaths/min), fever up to 39 C, Glasgow Coma Scale <8, and intermittent convulsions requiring endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.
objective.routine_investigations: Serial blood cultures remained negative (reported negative on March 2). Laboratory testing showed anemia, abnormal liver and renal function, abnormal coagulation, and multiorgan dysfunction. Initial TTE and TEE showed normal mechanical aortic valve function but revealed an aortic root abscess ulceration with multiple vegetations, localized aortic root entrapment with aneurysm, and segmental ventricular wall motion abnormalities.
objective.advanced_workup: Cranial CT showed prior cerebral infarction followed on February 20 by a right frontal lobe hematoma, right occipital subarachnoid hemorrhage, and multiple lacunar infarctions in the bilateral basal ganglia and left paraventricular area. Pulmonary CT showed bronchitis, and bronchoscopy revealed normal bronchial mucosa with scant thin yellow-white sputum. Serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan (G test) was elevated at 343.84 pg/mL and serum galactomannan (GM) was elevated at 0.83. Blood ultra-multiplex PCR (February 25) detected Aspergillus flavus (<1 x 10^2/L), Aspergillus oryzae (<1 x 10^2/L), and cytomegalovirus (2 x 10^2/L). Blood pathogen-targeted metagenomic next-generation sequencing (ptNGS) confirmed Aspergillus flavus (87 copies/mL) and Aspergillus oryzae (25 copies/mL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Prosthetic valve infective endocarditis with aortic root abscess and mycotic aneurysm caused by Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus oryzae, complicated by recurrent embolic cerebral infarctions and intracranial hemorrhage, confirmed by blood ultra-multiplex PCR, blood ptNGS, elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan (343.84 pg/mL) and galactomannan (0.83), and TEE findings despite negative conventional blood cultures. Treated with mechanical ventilation, sodium valproate, daptomycin, imipenem/cilastatin, and targeted intravenous voriconazole (6 mg/kg loading twice daily, then 4 mg/kg maintenance), achieving defervescence (37.8 C by February 28), extubation, recovery of consciousness, and transfer out of the ICU; however, the patient later died of a massive cerebral hemorrhage combined with a new cerebral infarction.
